pll1d28c7-d1e3501.summary: Notes that although 'Image' is said relatively of the Son, it is sometimes found said by substance.

pll1d28c7-d1e3504.summary: Cites Augustine: the divinity of the Trinity is essentially one, and is the image to which man was made.
claims: The Trinity's one divinity is the image to which man was made.

pll1d28c7-d1e3517.summary: Cites Hilary, De Trinitate V: man is made to the common image; the name does not differ, nor the nature; there is one form to which man was created. So 'image' sometimes signifies essence and is then said 'ad se.'
claims: Man is made to a common image of the one nature.

pl-l1d28c7.summary: Notes that 'Image,' though said relatively of the Son, is sometimes said by substance: Augustine says the divinity of the Trinity is essentially one and the image to which man was made, and Hilary says man was made to a common image of one nature. So 'image' sometimes signifies essence and is then said 'ad se.'
claims: 'Image' is usually said relatively of the Son.
Sometimes 'image' is said by substance, as the image of the whole Trinity to which man was made.
Man was made to the common image of the one divine nature.
